fields.description: Master switch for the whole marketing module. While off, no connector runs and no scheduled job does any work. Every per-platform flag below is additionally required — this one alone turns nothing on.
fields.label: Enable Marketing Module

fields.description: Pull campaigns and daily metrics from Google Ads. Requires an approved developer token with Basic Access — see docs/marketing-platform-approvals.md.
fields.label: Google Ads

fields.description: Pull campaigns and daily metrics from Meta Ads. Requires the ads_read permission from Meta App Review.
fields.label: Meta Ads

fields.description: Pull campaigns and daily metrics from LinkedIn Ads. Requires Marketing Developer Platform access, historically the slowest approval of the set — if it never clears, LinkedIn spend goes in as offline Marketing Spend rows instead.
fields.label: LinkedIn Ads

fields.description: Whether an approved post may go out to each network. All ship off. Switching one on never skips approval: nothing is queued until a post has an approver. Takes effect only once that network's publisher is installed and its account is connected.
fields.label: Publishing (posts to public accounts)

fields.description: Post to the Facebook Page. Requires Meta App Review for pages_manage_posts.
fields.label: Facebook Page

fields.description: Post to the Instagram business account linked to the Page. Requires Meta App Review for instagram_content_publish.
fields.label: Instagram

fields.description: Post as the Company Page. Requires LinkedIn Community Management API access.
fields.label: LinkedIn Company Page

fields.description: Upload to the YouTube channel. Until the YouTube Data API audit passes, every video uploaded through the API is locked private, and that lock cannot be appealed.
fields.label: YouTube

fields.description: The Marketing Performance page's other sources (v1.756.0). Each pulls nightly only while the master switch above is on as well, and only once its connection is made.
fields.label: Marketing Performance

fields.description: Read the Google Business Profile listing's daily calls, website clicks, direction requests and impressions, and its reviews. Google must approve API access first; connect it on Marketing Connections.
fields.label: Google Business Profile

fields.description: Read followers, reach and views for each enabled Social Account, through its publishing connection. Read-only; publishing stays behind its own switches.
fields.label: Social Page Stats

fields.description: One per line. A Search Console query containing any of these (case and spaces ignored) counts as branded on the Marketing Performance page.
fields.label: Branded Search Terms

fields.description: The marketing reports, the Marketing Performance page's flags, and the alerts (v1.757.0). Every figure ships with a working default, so nothing here is off until someone sets it.
fields.label: Insights

fields.description: Near Page One (R3) lists a query or page only with at least this many impressions in the range.
fields.label: Near Page One: Minimum Impressions

fields.description: Fading Pages (R4): a page counts as fading when its clicks fell by at least this percent.
fields.label: Fading Pages: Drop (%)

fields.description: Fading Pages (R4) ignores a page under this many clicks in the period it is compared with, so small pages do not flap.
fields.label: Fading Pages: Minimum Baseline Clicks

fields.description: Missed Calls (R6): an unanswered incoming call counts as missed when nobody called the number back within this many hours.
fields.label: Missed Calls: Callback Window (hours)

fields.description: Service Line Funnel (R5): rules tried in order, the first match wins. Seeded with Sapphire's value streams and likely page and query words; edit to fit the site.
fields.label: Service Lines

fields.description: Sent to every enabled user holding one of the alert roles, nightly at 06:15 and never more than once per throttle window for the same thing.
fields.label: Alerts

fields.description: Ships unticked, so the alerts run from day one: a sharp drop, a key page out of Google, a bad review or a missed first-time call should reach somebody. Tick to stop them all.
fields.label: Pause Marketing Alerts

fields.description: One role per line. Service accounts and Administrator are never sent to.
fields.label: Alert Roles

fields.description: The same alert goes again only after this many hours.
fields.label: Throttle (hours)

fields.description: Alert when last week's sessions or search clicks fell this percent or more against the week before.
fields.label: Weekly Drop (%)

fields.description: Only from a week before of at least this many sessions (or search clicks), so a quiet week cannot alarm.
fields.label: Weekly Drop: Minimum Baseline

fields.description: Alert on a new Google review at this many stars or fewer. 0 turns this alert off.
fields.label: Low Review (stars)

fields.description: One full address per line. Checked nightly with Search Console's URL Inspection (2,000 a day allowed; keep this short), and an alert goes when Google stops indexing one.
fields.label: Key Pages

fields.description: How many trailing days to re-pull on every run. Platforms revise spend and conversion figures after the fact, so the last complete day is not final. The (campaign, date) key makes a re-pull an upsert rather than a duplicate.
fields.label: Restate Trailing Days

fields.description: How far back an ad account's first sync reads. Since v1.756.0 never less than the platform keeps daily figures for (37 months at Google Ads and Meta, six months at LinkedIn; core/constants.HISTORY_DAYS), so this only matters set higher.
fields.label: Initial Backfill Days

fields.description: Attempts per request before a run is marked Failed. Applies to retryable responses only — 429 and 5xx. A 403 is a configuration fault and is never retried.
fields.label: Max Retries

fields.description: Per-request HTTP timeout in seconds.
fields.label: Request Timeout (seconds)

fields.description: Rows written per commit when ingesting daily metrics.
fields.label: Sync Batch Size

fields.description: How long to keep Marketing Raw Payload rows. The archive is for debugging a mapper against what the platform actually sent; it is not a data store and it grows quickly.
fields.label: Raw Payload Retention (days)

fields.description: Summary of the most recent run. Per-account connection state lives on Ad Account, and the per-run detail is in Marketing Sync Log.
fields.label: Last Sync Status
